From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Folks —

Prelim notes from the first pass on traces (attached trace_dump_0522.log):
- Root cause correlates with catalog refresh v2026-05-22: new default quantization profile selected for small-seq attention paths. On a subset of GPUs (A100p in us-west-2 pooled nodes) we’re falling back to a slower kernel due to buffer alignment changes.
- The increased tail latency is concentrated on short requests (<= 64 tokens) which FinLytics heavily uses. p50 unaffected; p95/p99 inflated by 8–10x for these short requests.
- No memory pressure or OOMs; CPU and GPU utilization unchanged. Not a burst/queueing issue.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Roll back the catalog variant for hosted us-west-2 to v2026-05-19 (fastest).
2) Push a hotfix to the runtime kernel selector to force the previous quantization path for small sequences (non-disruptive but needs canary).
3) Route FinLytics traffic to dedicated nodes with pinned kernel path (temporary, higher-cost).

I recommend (1) for fastest customer relief while we prepare (2) for a controlled rollout. I’ll prepare a rollback playbook and a canary for the hotfix.

Markus — we’ll need approval to rollback the catalog in hosted for the affected pool and to notify impacted customers.

-Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
